name: Omapager
author: Neil Patel
description: Notifications for Omarchy: a stacking, grouping replacement for the built-in service, with markup parsing, resolved source icons, inline reply, and per-source snooze.

barWidget.description: Appears only when notifications are being held back: crossed-out bell when silenced, zzz when a source is snoozed. Click silences, right-click opens a panel to wake sources or snooze them for longer.

schema.label: Live notifications stack
schema.description: all = one deck in the corner, same-source notifications grouped inside it; source = a separate deck per source, each expanding on its own.

schema.label: Notification buttons
schema.description: Which end of a card its action buttons sit at.

schema.label: Hide the browser's Settings button
schema.description: Chrome puts a Settings action on every web notification. It is the same button on every card and it crowds out the ones that are worth pressing.

schema.label: Snooze lengths
schema.description: What the snooze menus offer, on a card and in the panel. A desktop where half an hour is the useful unit and one where half a day is are both real.

schema.label: Tomorrow morning starts at
schema.description: The hour "until tomorrow" wakes a source at, on a 24-hour clock.

schema.label: Sources listed in the panel
schema.description: How many quietened sources the panel lists at once. A fortnight of silence should not turn it into a log file.

schema.label: Held notifications shown per source
schema.description: How many of the notifications a source held back the panel will show when you open it.

schema.label: Always show
schema.description: Keep the slot in the bar even when nothing is being held back. The icon appearing is the one moment the bar's centre shifts; this trades a permanently dim bell for a clock that never moves.

schema.label: Let verification codes through
schema.description: A snooze or a silence holds everything back except a notification carrying a verification code. You asked for that code thirty seconds ago and it expires in five minutes, so "I'll look later" does not apply to it.

schema.label: Clock
schema.description: How wake times are written. system follows LC_TIME; Omarchy's own clock widget takes an explicit format string instead, so pin this if the two disagree.
